title: How do we construct a rectangle made of three identical squares?
description: A rectangle that splits into three identical squares is constructed by choosing a square side of three centimetres and copying it along the base with the compass. Keeko's doubt is that the rectangle is twice as long as it is wide.
teaching_notes: One idea: a rectangle made of three identical squares has a length of three square sides, which is three times its breadth. Watch for students who carry over the idea of twice from the two-square rectangle.

source: Construct a rectangle that can be divided into 3 identical s
video_script.why: A learner constructs a rectangle that splits into three identical squares by choosing a square side and copying it with the compass.
video_script.substitution: the book's own rectangle split by two upright lines into three identical squares, with a chosen side of three centimetres
video_script.anchor: a rectangle split by two upright lines into three identical squares
video_script.wrong_answer: the rectangle is twice as long as it is wide
video_script.wrong_move: carries over the two-square rectangle and makes the length twice the breadth, so only two squares fit
video_script.payoff_line: The length must be three times the breadth.

final_answer.value: Any rectangle whose length is 3 times its breadth, for example 9 cm by 3 cm. Each square has side 3 cm

maths_rules: no measurements are given, so choose the square side: 3 cm
first square: AB = 3 cm, perpendiculars at A and B, AD = BC = 3 cm
the compass copies 3 cm twice more along the base: 3 cm + 3 cm + 3 cm = 9 cm
length = 9 cm = 3 times the breadth 3 cm; each of the three parts is a 3 cm square
video_script.design: One square is drawn, its side is copied twice with the compass, and the rectangle is closed and checked.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the rectangle is twice as long as it is wide.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But twice the width holds only two squares, and the third square does not fit.
<bookmark mark='keep'/>Three squares need three times the width, which is nine centimetres here.
